mainTopic: Wine touched by a non-Jew without intent: רבא's leniency is refuted by אביי's sources, and two תנאים disagree about wine poured by a hidden non-Jew.
overview: רב הונא בריה דרב נחמן visits מחוזא, where רבא had allowed a barrel of wine stirred by a non-Jew to be sold. In private, רבא says such wine is forbidden even for הנאה. He explains that he only allowed the money from the rest of the barrel, not the value of the forbidden wine itself. רבא then recalls how אביי (נחמני) pressed him with sources forbidding such wine: rulings of שמואל in נהרדעא and רבי יוחנן in טבריא, and a ברייתא about a non-Jewish market inspector who tasted wine. רבא tries to push these aside, but אביי points out that the same ברייתא says 'it may be sold' when it means only drinking is forbidden. The גמרא declares רבא fully refuted. Next comes a story where a man pouring wine for two תנאים turned out to be a non-Jew. One forbade the wine even for הנאה, and the other permitted it even for drinking. רבי יהושע בן לוי says both ruled well, and his reasons continue on the next amud.

steps.title: רב הונא arrives and רבא asks for privacy
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נחמן comes to מחוזא. רבא tells his attendant to shut the gates so they can talk without interruption.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נחמן came to מחוזא. רבא told his attendant רב אליקים: Close the gates, so that people who would disturb us do not come in.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a story opening that sets the scene. The גמרא is preparing for the private discussion about the stirred wine that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had earlier ruled in מחוזא about wine a non-Jew stirred. Now a sage who may question that ruling has arrived. רבא arranges a quiet meeting so the matter can be clarified without crowds.

phrases.aramaic: אִיקְּלַע רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן לְמָחוֹזָא,
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Nachman happened to come to Mechoza.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב אֶלְיָקִים שַׁמָּעֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Elyakim, his attendant:

phrases.aramaic: טְרוֹק גַּלֵּי, דְּלָא נֵיתוֹ אִינָשֵׁי דְּנִיטְרֹיד.
phrases.english: Close the gates, so that people who would disturb us do not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיקְּלַע רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן לְמָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story connected to רבא's earlier ruling on stirred wine in מחוזא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רבא arranges a private meeting with רב הונא בריה דרב נחמן.

steps.title: רב הונא asks what the law is in this case
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא goes in to רבא and asks what the הלכה is in a case like this one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went in to him and said to him: In a case like this, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks רבא directly what the law is for wine a non-Jew stirred without meaning to offer it to an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'a case like this' point back to the real case in מחוזא. The question tests whether רבא really holds that such wine is permitted.

phrases.english: He went in to him and said to him:
In a case like this, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means the case of wine stirred by a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The private meeting set up in step 1 begins with this question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the status of wine that a non-Jew stirred?

steps.title: רבא: forbidden even for benefit
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that such wine is forbidden even for הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden even to benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a strict answer. You may not drink the wine, and you may not even make money from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds stricter than what רבא seemed to allow in מחוזא, where he let the wine be sold. That apparent clash sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: forbidden for any benefit, including selling

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden even for benefit.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wine stirred by a non-Jew is forbidden even for benefit.

steps.title: But you said stirring does not make it libation wine
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא challenges רבא with his own earlier statement that stirring does not turn wine into יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it you, Master, who said: Stirring does not make wine into libation wine!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא points out that רבא's answer seems to contradict something רבא himself said before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If stirring does not create יין נסך, the wine should be permitted for benefit. That is how רבא allowed its sale. So how can he now say it is forbidden even for benefit?

keyTerms.meaning: but wasn't it you, Master, who said
wine poured for idol worship, forbidden for benefit

phrases.english: But wasn't it the Master who said:
If he stirred it, he does not make it libation wine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 3 using רבא's own earlier words.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that stirred wine is forbidden for benefit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction: רבא said elsewhere that stirring does not create יין נסך, which implies the wine is permitted for benefit.

steps.title: רבא: I never allowed the value of the touched wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that he allowed only the value of the rest of the barrel, not the value of the wine that was actually involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that I said it is permitted apart from the value of that wine. Did I say the value of that wine itself is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction. His permission to sell covered only part of the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the wine is sold, the money equal to the forbidden wine itself must not be used. Only the rest of the proceeds may be enjoyed. So 'forbidden for benefit' applies to that wine, and the sale is still allowed for the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: say that what I said was

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not taking back his ruling. He is clarifying it: selling was allowed, but the money matching the forbidden wine itself stays forbidden.

phrases.english: Say that what I said was:
apart from the value of that wine.
phrases.notes: "That wine" is the forbidden wine that got into the barrel.

phrases.english: The value of that wine, did I say it was permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the earlier statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא permitted benefit from the entire stirred barrel.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the proceeds beyond the value of the forbidden wine are permitted. The value of that wine itself is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the barrel may be sold, but the money equal to the forbidden wine itself may not be used.

steps.title: אביי surrounded רבא with sources forbidding it
steps.stepSummary: רבא recalls that in פומבדיתא, אביי (נחמני) confronted him with amoraic traditions and a ברייתא forbidding stirred wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When I came to פומבדיתא, נחמני surrounded us with traditions and a ברייתא saying that it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts telling about an earlier debate. The גמרא is setting up the sources that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחמני is a name for אביי. He brought two kinds of sources against רבא's lenient view: rulings of אמוראים (שמעתתא) and a teaching of תנאים (מתניתא). The rulings are listed right away, in the following steps.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a Torah center in בבל
a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים

phrases.english: Rava said: When I came to Pumbedita,
Nachmani surrounded us with traditions and a baraita that it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the current ruling to רבא's memory of an earlier debate with אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי had both amoraic and tannaitic sources forbidding stirred wine.

steps.title: שמואל and רבי יוחנן both forbade it
steps.stepSummary: The amoraic traditions: שמואל forbade stirred wine in a case in נהרדעא, and רבי יוחנן did the same in טבריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The traditions: there was a case in נהרדעא and שמואל forbade it, and in טבריא רבי יוחנן forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא lists the first kind of source אביי brought: real cases where great אמוראים forbade wine a non-Jew stirred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two leading אמוראים, one in בבל and one in ארץ ישראל, ruled strictly in actual cases. That is strong proof against רבא's leniency.

phrases.english: The traditions: that case which happened in Nehardea,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲסַר שְׁמוּאֵל, בִּטְבֶרְיָא וַאֲסַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: and Shmuel forbade it; in Tiberias, and Rabbi Yochanan forbade it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'traditions' mentioned in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: Wine stirred by a non-Jew is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Actual rulings of שמואל in נהרדעא and רבי יוחנן in טבריא.

steps.title: רבא: they were strict because the people were unlearned
steps.stepSummary: רבא answered that those rulings were extra strictness, since the people there were not בני תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to him: Because they are not people of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's proof. He says those rulings were special strictness for those towns, not the basic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlearned people might take a lenient ruling too far. So שמואל and רבי יוחנן forbade the wine to keep them away from sin. Where people are learned, no such fence is needed.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַרִי לֵיהּ: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָן בְּנֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: And I said to him: Because they are not people of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרִי לֵיהּ: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָן בְּנֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 7 by limiting those rulings to special local conditions.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the rulings of שמואל and רבי יוחנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Those rulings were a protective fence for unlearned people, not the basic law.

steps.title: אביי: is מחוזא more learned than טבריא and נהרדעא?
steps.stepSummary: אביי mocked the idea that the great Torah towns of טבריא and נהרדעא were unlearned while מחוזא was learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to me: טבריא and נהרדעא are not people of Torah, and מחוזא is people of Torah?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רבא's answer with a sharp rhetorical question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבריא and נהרדעא were famous centers of Torah. If those towns needed a strict fence, מחוזא surely did too. So רבא should not have been lenient in מחוזא even by his own reasoning.

phrases.english: And he said to me:
Tiberias and Nehardea are not people of Torah,
while those of Mechoza are people of Torah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לִי: טְבֶרְיָא וּנְהַרְדְּעָא אֵינָן בְּנֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's answer from step 8, bringing back the force of the proof in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's claim that the strict rulings applied only to unlearned towns.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: טבריא and נהרדעא were no less learned than מחוזא, so the same strictness should apply in מחוזא.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's point: the strict rulings of שמואל and רבי יוחנן cannot be pushed aside as fences for unlearned people, because those towns were Torah centers.

steps.title: The barrel-tasting market inspector
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא where the חכמים forbade wine that a גוי market inspector tasted, and suggests it means forbidden even for הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא: a non-Jewish market inspector drilled into a barrel with a tube and drew wine up, or tasted wine from a cup and poured the rest back into the barrel. This really happened, and the חכמים forbade the wine. Doesn't that mean it was forbidden even for benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a third source against רבא, after the rulings of שמואל and רבי יוחנן. This time it is a ברייתא, and he reads it as forbidding the wine even for הנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inspector did not mean to make a נסך. He only wanted to taste or check the wine. Even so, the חכמים forbade it. If 'forbade' means forbidden even for הנאה, that goes against רבא, who allowed people to benefit from wine touched without intent.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים (here, a ברייתא)
A market inspector who checks measures and prices
A tube or siphon for drawing liquid
Benefit, such as selling the wine or using it in another way besides drinking

phrases.english: A baraita:
In the case of a gentile market inspector
who drilled a hole with a tube and drew wine up
or who tasted from the cup
and poured the rest back into the barrel
This was an actual incident, and they forbade it.
Does it not mean forbidden even for benefit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the attack on רבא's answer about the amoraic traditions, אביי moves on to the ברייתא he mentioned in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That wine touched by a גוי without intent is forbidden even for הנאה, against רבא

steps.title: Only drinking was forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא forbade only drinking, not benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it was forbidden only for drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes away the proof. He says the word 'forbade' in the ברייתא means only that the wine may not be drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ruling is only about drinking, selling the wine would still be allowed. That fits רבא's view, so the ברייתא is no longer a problem for him.

phrases.english: No, it means forbidden for drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the inference that 'forbade' includes הנאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Forbade' can just mean forbidden to drink

steps.title: The same ברייתא says 'it may be sold' when it wants to
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that the ברייתא's last case says 'יִמָּכֵר' when only drinking is forbidden, so 'forbade' in the first case must mean more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said 'it may be sold,' the way the last part says: a non-Jewish confiscator put his hand into a barrel thinking it held oil, and it turned out to be wine. This really happened, and they said: 'It may be sold.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's answer by pointing to the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the ברייתא wants to allow selling, it says so clearly: 'יִמָּכֵר'. In the first case it only says 'they forbade it', with no permission to sell. That shows the wine there was forbidden even for הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: It may be sold (benefit allowed, drinking forbidden)
The latter clause of a teaching
A confiscator, an official who seizes property

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases are touching without intent to make a נסך. The confiscator, though, did not even know the barrel held wine. That is why the ruling there is lighter ('it may be sold') than in the inspector's case.

phrases.english: If so, let it teach 'it may be sold'
as the latter clause teaches:
a gentile confiscator
who stretched his hand into the barrel
thinking it was a barrel of oil
and it turned out to be of wine
This was an actual incident, and they said: 'It may be sold.'

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that 'forbade' means forbidden only for drinking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same ברייתא says 'it may be sold' when only drinking is forbidden. Since it does not say that here, the wine must be forbidden even for benefit.

steps.title: רבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a full refutation of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבא, a full refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that רבא's position cannot stand against this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is given to the point about 'יִמָּכֵר'. So רבא's lenient ruling from earlier in the סוגיא is rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: Wine a גוי drew out or tasted and poured back, even without meaning to make a נסך, is forbidden even for הנאה. Only when he did not know it was wine at all (the חרם) may it be sold.

phrases.english: The refutation of Rava is a conclusive refutation.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's leniency is refuted. Such wine is forbidden even for הנאה.

steps.title: Two תנאים served wine by a hidden גוי
steps.stepSummary: A man poured wine for רבי יוחנן בן ארזא and רבי יוסי בן נהוראי and was then found to be a גוי. One forbade the wine even for הנאה, the other permitted it even for drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ארזא and רבי יוסי בן נהוראי were sitting and drinking wine. A certain man came, and they said to him: 'Come, pour for us.' After he poured into the cup, it turned out he was a non-Jew. One forbade the wine even for benefit, and one permitted it even for drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a case of wine touched by a גוי, where two תנאים ruled in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man only poured, and he poured at the Jews' request. The question is whether that counts as touching the wine in a way that makes it forbidden. The two rulings are as far apart as possible: one says even הנאה is forbidden, the other says even drinking is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן אַרְזָא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן נְהוֹרַאי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Arza and Rabbi Yosei ben Nehorai
were sitting and drinking wine.
A certain man came.
They said to him: Come, pour drinks for us.
After he poured the wine into the cup
it was revealed that he was a gentile.
One forbade it even for benefit,
and one permitted it even for drinking.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן אַרְזָא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן נְהוֹרַאי הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about the same topic of wine handled by a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute between the two תנאים: forbidden even for הנאה, or permitted even for drinking.

steps.title: Both opinions are valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says each תנא ruled well, and he starts to explain the one who forbade.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The one who forbade ruled well, and the one who permitted ruled well. The one who forbade...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי says both rulings make sense. The last words begin his explanation, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not pick a winner. He says each side has a real reason, and he is about to give the reasoning behind each one, starting with the one who forbade.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The one who forbade forbade properly,
and the one who permitted permitted properly.
The one who forbade —
phrases.notes: His reason comes right after this, at the start of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מַאן דְּאָסַר שַׁפִּיר אָסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the dispute in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both rulings are reasonable. The explanation of each begins here.
